questions.question_text: Use the formal algorithm to calculate $312 \times 3$.

options.why: Multiplied only the ones digit and left the other digits unchanged.
Reversed the product digits after working from right to left.
Used 5 instead of 6 for the ones-column product.

questions.question_text: Use the formal algorithm to calculate $58 \times 7$.

options.why: Forgot to add the carried 5 to the tens-column product.
Wrote the carried 5 as the final ones digit instead of 6.
Added the two separate digit-products instead of combining place values.
Did not add either carried digit to the next column.
Added the first carry but omitted the carry into the hundreds column.
Added one extra hundred when combining the final carry.

questions.question_text: Use the formal algorithm to calculate $3027 \times 4$.

options.why: Failed to carry 2 from the ones column into the tens column.
Inserted an extra zero for the zero hundreds digit.
Multiplied the tens digit but omitted the carried 2.
Ignored the carried 3 from the ones-column product of 30.
Added the carried 3 after choosing the tens digit rather than within its product.
Copied the tens digit of the final product into the missing place.

questions.question_text: In $689 \times 7$, what happens immediately after calculating $9 \times 7=63$?

options.text: Write $3$ in the ones column and carry $6$
Write $6$ in the ones column and carry $3$
options.why: Reversed the written digit and the carried tens digit.

options.text: Write $63$ in the ones column and carry nothing
options.why: Placed a two-digit product into a single place-value column.

options.text: Write $3$ in the ones column and discard $6$
options.why: Recorded the ones digit but lost the tens that must be carried.

questions.solution_text:
$9 \times 7=63$.
Write $3$ in the ones column and carry $6$ to the tens column.

questions.question_text: A student gives $572 \times 8=4516$. Which statement identifies the first error?

options.why: Used an incorrect basic fact; 2 times 8 is 16, not 14.
Used an incorrect basic fact; 5 times 8 is 40, before adding the carry.

options.text: The digits should be multiplied from left to right
options.why: Reversed the required algorithm direction, which begins in the ones column.
